data.why: The repo ships data/results.csv and data/curves.npz, the precomputed scores and light-curve arrays that app.py reads directly; the dashboard has no upload widget and does no live inference, so nothing needs to be supplied or written.

goals: Pick a KOI signal and read the model's planet-probability verdict alongside its global and local light-curve views
Compare a signal's predicted score against its ground-truth label to see whether the model got it right
Filter to only the model's misclassifications to spot where the classifier is unreliable
Check aggregate reliability metrics (PR-AUC, ROC-AUC) on the held-out test set
Tune the decision threshold on the confusion matrix to see the precision/recall tradeoff
Inspect the distribution of scores by true class to judge class separability

review.summary: The tree states the dashboard's purpose correctly: vetting a 1D-CNN's planet/false-signal calls on Kepler KOIs one at a time and across the test set. Its phases, labels and seven features match app.py, and every screen I sampled shows what its node says. It needs small fixes before filing: add a 'diagnose a misclassification from its curves' task, remove a little overlap between tasks, fix the header-card placement, and repair check.json's screen references, which don't match this folder.
